newsitem.title: CANADA: GOLF-HEALTHY BURTON CLOSES IN ON DU MARUIER LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HEALTHY BURTON CLOSES IN ON DU MARUIER LEAD.

text.p: Brandie Burton, whose career has been plagued by illness and injury, fired a seven-under-par 66 at the du Maurier Classic Saturday to vault into contention for her second title in the LPGA's final major tournament of the year.

A day after celebrating her 25th birthday, the 1993 du Maurier champion carded eight birdies to reach nine-under-par 210, a score that left her just one stroke back of third-round leader Kelly Robbins.
Robbins, who grabbed the lead Friday with a sparkling 65, lost her chance to pull away from her pursuers by shooting just even-par 73 Saturday.
Juli Inkster was tied with Burton for second after a two-under 71, with Sweden's Liselotte Neumann and Rosie Jones another stroke back at eight-under 211.
Briton Laura Davies pretty much ruled out her chances of a successful defence after a 73 that left her at 216.
Davies came from five behind on the final day to win at Edmonton last year, but asked if she thought she could close a seven-shot gap, she said: "I wouldn't hold your breath."

Burton has four victories from her seven years on the LPGA Tour, but none since 1993. Since then she has been busy recovering from knee surgeries, jaw operations, a bad wrist, a sore back and a broken rib.
"I've had so many injuries in my career, that's it hard to keep up," she said.

"Ribs, wrist, back, and I've had jaw surgery for a degenerative condition called TMJ three times, most recently in January. I've also had surgery on my knee three times, I'm a bit of a physical wreck.
"But I'm 100% healthy right now, which I haven't been at this stage of the season for years. Perhaps, at last, I'm learning that you can't play seven weeks in a row and stay healthy."
Burton enjoyed a hot day with her putter after receiving a tip from former Ryder Cup captain Dave Stockton.
"I telephoned him last night, and he suggested I think about keeping my left arm straight through the stroke."
It certainly worked as she twice holed from 25 feet -- at the 12th and 18th -- from 20 feet on the third hole and three more from better than 10 feet.
Robbins, who stands third on the LPGA money list, was clearly frustrated with her level par round. It was only her birdie on the par-5 18th that kept her in sole possession of the lead.
She got to 11 under with a birdie at the long fifth, but immediately handed it back and dropped another stroke at the 10th.
"There wasn't much going on for me out there," said Robbins, who is seeking her third title of the year.
